second_order: building, rebuilding, and keeping the South African flag going
theme_note: These passages recruit painters and do the shared flag work: starting it, joining it, reporting coordinates and progress, maintaining it, moving it, and declaring a build done. What varies is whether the work is a first build, a rebuild after loss, routine maintenance, or a small move.
regrouped_from: Split from fixing the flag pixel by pixel: these codes mobilise or sustain the shared build, while the separated theme handles concrete corrections to shape, colour, lettering, and templates.

second_order: choosing whether to fight, talk, or move when pixels are under pressure
theme_note: These codes weigh and announce responses to overwriting or crowding: diplomacy, attack, retreat, relocation, covert takeover, defence, or acknowledging loss. What varies is the named threat and the chosen response; the common practice is deciding what to do when the drawing is pressured.
regrouped_from: Split from dealing with neighbouring flags: shared adjacency did not make one practice. These codes decide how to answer pressure; the neighbour theme records bargains, reciprocal help, and boundaries.

theme_note: These passages turn territorial work into jokes about embassies, fika, rooibos, walls, Lesotho, spam, colonials, and a lettering battle. The targets and joke forms vary, but each makes the canvas fight into a shared joke rather than a practical instruction alone.

second_order: bargaining for space and trading help with neighbouring flags
theme_note: These codes negotiate permission, borders, shared space, mutual defence, alliance membership, and requests for help with other drawings. What varies is the counterpart and whether the exchange ends in agreement, refusal, or simple assistance; the common practice is reciprocal dealing with visible neighbours or visiting groups.
regrouped_from: Split from fighting or moving under pressure because a neighbour being named is not itself a shared practice: these passages make offers, bargains, permissions, boundaries, and reciprocal commitments.

second_order: moving faster coordination into Discord and chat
theme_note: These passages create, share, or direct painters into Discord or chat for coordination. The venue and level of visible activity vary, while the shared practice is moving some organising away from the subreddit.

second_order: trying to start the subreddit's own April Fools hoax
theme_note: This single exchange proposes a local hoax, says the proposal came too late, and invokes the after-noon rule. It belongs with no canvas practice because participants are discussing their own April Fools conduct, not drawing on r/place.

second_order: fixing colours, proportions, letters, and templates pixel by pixel
theme_note: These passages diagnose and repair concrete design details: proportions, templates, stripe widths, reversed colours, heart repairs, letter spacing, and fit beside other pixels. What varies is the object being corrected and whether the correction is accepted, mistaken, or disputed.
regrouped_from: Split from building and keeping the flag going because these codes do the fine-grained corrective work rather than recruiting or sustaining the build as a whole.

second_order: pulling scattered pixel talk into a sticky megathread
theme_note: These codes ask for one sticky, report that moderators were already asked, create the coordination megathread, and redirect later proposals into it. The speakers vary between members and a moderator, while the practice is consolidating scattered work in one subreddit thread.

second_order: proposing words and pictures beyond the flag
theme_note: These passages propose labels, banners, landmarks, political images, and other additions beyond maintaining the flag itself. The proposed content varies widely, and several proposals are rejected or left unanswered; what holds them together is asking the room to add another named image or phrase to the canvas.

second_order: saying they wing it and go with the flow
theme_note: These passages contrast an inactive Discord with participants doing their own thing, then name the local method as winging it and going with the flow. They form a practice-specific account of loose coordination rather than evidence that organising moved successfully into Discord.
regrouped_from: Lifted out of the Discord theme because the shared words describe not using central organisation, which is the opposite practice from moving coordination into a venue.

second_order: arguing over whether pixel work belongs here
theme_note: These passages call pixel posts spam or a one-off game, defend them as a way to unite away from street politics, demand that they stay in one thread, or dismiss the work as less important. Positions vary, but the shared practice is contesting the place and value of r/place activity in the subreddit.

second_order: using an automatic repair script until it fights the new plan
theme_note: One passage shares automation to repair flag blemishes and another asks users to update it after the script begins undoing changed plans. Together they show the same repair tool first helping and then conflicting with current human instructions.

second_order: celebrating, mourning, and revisiting what they made
theme_note: These passages mark what the shared pixels meant and look back after placement: mourning the ending, celebrating having made a name, congratulating participants, recalling a Lego flag, watching a timelapse, revising a joke about it, and directing viewers to the finished area. What varies is celebration, loss, recollection, and visual wayfinding.
regrouped_from: Kept separate from live building after reviewing the late slices: post-event recall and viewing are a different practice from coordinating pixels while placement remained open.

second_order: following a flag story into questions about working at Google
theme_note: After the Lego-flag story, commenters ask whether the maker worked at Google and how the job came about, and the author answers. These turns belong together as a closed question-and-answer detour from the flag story and with no other canvas practice.
